questions.prompt: Which of the following is a derived quantity?
questions.explanation: Area = length × length, so it is built from a base quantity and is therefore derived. Length, mass and time are fundamental quantities.

questions.prompt: In which of these can sound NOT travel?
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave and needs a material (medium) to travel through. A vacuum has no particles, so sound cannot pass through it.

questions.prompt: An image formed in a flat (plane) mirror is always:
questions.explanation: A plane mirror forms a virtual, upright image the same size as the object and as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.prompt: Two objects carry the same kind of charge. The force between them is:
questions.explanation: Like charges repel and unlike charges attract. Two objects with the same kind of charge therefore push each other apart (repulsion).

questions.prompt: Which quantity does a voltmeter measure in a circuit?
questions.explanation: A voltmeter measures the potential difference (voltage) across a component, in volts. Current is measured by an ammeter and resistance by an ohmmeter.

questions.prompt: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth across empty space?
questions.explanation: Radiation transfers heat as infrared waves and needs no medium, so it can cross the vacuum of space. Conduction and convection both need matter.

questions.prompt: A rectangular plate measures 0.5 m by 0.4 m. What is its area in square metres?
questions.explanation: Area = length × width = 0.5 m × 0.4 m = 0.2 m².

questions.prompt: A train starts from rest and reaches 30 m/s in 15 s. What is its acceleration?

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A 2.5 kg object is dropped near the Earth. Taking g = 10 m/s², what is its weight?
questions.explanation: Weight W = mg = 2.5 kg × 10 m/s² = 25 N.

questions.prompt: A force of 25 N pushes a box 8 m along the floor in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work W = F × d = 25 N × 8 m = 200 J.

questions.prompt: A block of metal has a mass of 1.5 kg and a volume of 0.0002 m³. What is its density?
questions.explanation: Density = mass ÷ volume = 1.5 ÷ 0.0002 = 7500 kg/m³.

questions.prompt: Convert 250 K into degrees Celsius.
A wave has a speed of 360 m/s and a frequency of 90 Hz. What is its wavelength?
questions.explanation: From v = fλ, wavelength λ = v ÷ f = 360 ÷ 90 = 4 m.

questions.prompt: A ray of light hits a plane mirror with an angle of incidence of 40° (measured from the normal). What is the angle of reflection?
questions.explanation: By the law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, so it is 40°.

questions.prompt: A 12 V battery is connected across a 4 Ω resistor. What current flows?
questions.explanation: By Ohm's law I = V ÷ R = 12 ÷ 4 = 3 A.

questions.prompt: A plastic comb rubbed with a cloth becomes negatively charged. This happens because the comb has:
questions.explanation: Charging by friction transfers electrons. An object that becomes negative has gained electrons; protons in the nucleus do not move.

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: Two forces act on a box along the same line: 14 N to the right and 6 N to the left. What is the net force?
questions.explanation: Opposite forces subtract: 14 N − 6 N = 8 N, in the direction of the larger force, so 8 N to the right.

questions.prompt: A cyclist accelerates from 4 m/s at a constant 2 m/s² for 5 s. What distance does the cyclist cover?
A motor lifts a 20 kg load to a height of 6 m in 8 s (g = 10 m/s²). What is the useful power output?
Find the pressure at a depth of 12 m in sea water of density 1025 kg/m³ (g = 10 m/s²).
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure P = ρgh = 1025 × 10 × 12 = 123 000 Pa.

questions.prompt: A pot of boiling water at 100 °C and a cold drink at 4 °C are placed in a warm room at 25 °C. Which way does heat flow?
options: From the room into the boiling water
Out of the boiling water, and into the cold drink
From the cold drink into the room only
No heat flows because the room is in between
questions.explanation: Heat always flows from hotter to colder. The 100 °C water loses heat to the 25 °C room, while the 4 °C drink gains heat from the 25 °C room.

questions.prompt: A person shouts at a cliff and hears the echo 3 s later. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far away is the cliff?
questions.explanation: Total distance = speed × time = 340 × 3 = 1020 m. The sound travels to the cliff and back, so the cliff distance = 1020 ÷ 2 = 510 m.

questions.prompt: Two resistors of 3 Ω and 5 Ω are connected in series across a 16 V battery. What current flows in the circuit?
questions.explanation: Series resistances add: R = 3 + 5 = 8 Ω. Then I = V ÷ R = 16 ÷ 8 = 2 A.

questions.prompt: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror so that the angle between the incident ray and the reflected ray is 70°. What is the angle of incidence?
questions.explanation: The angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection, and together they make the 70° between the two rays. So each angle = 70 ÷ 2 = 35°.

questions.prompt: A wire has a length of 2.5 mm. Express this length in metres using scientific notation.

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A net force of 18 N gives a body an acceleration of 6 m/s². What is the mass of the body?
questions.explanation: From F = ma, mass m = F ÷ a = 18 ÷ 6 = 3 kg.

questions.prompt: A neutral metal sphere is touched by a positively charged rod and some electrons flow from the sphere to the rod. The sphere becomes:
questions.explanation: Losing electrons leaves the sphere with more protons than electrons, so it becomes positively charged. This is charging by contact (conduction).

questions.prompt: A 3 kg ball is dropped from a height of 5 m (g = 10 m/s²). Using energy conservation, what is its speed just before hitting the ground?
questions.explanation: PE at top = KE at bottom: mgh = ½mv², so v² = 2gh = 2 × 10 × 5 = 100, giving v = 10 m/s. (Mass cancels out.)

questions.prompt: A box has a weight of 600 N and its base measures 2 m by 1.5 m. What pressure does it exert on the floor?
questions.explanation: Base area = 2 × 1.5 = 3 m². Pressure P = F ÷ A = 600 ÷ 3 = 200 Pa.

questions.prompt: A car moving at 20 m/s decelerates uniformly and stops after travelling 50 m. What is the magnitude of its deceleration?
questions.explanation: Use v² = u² + 2as with v = 0: 0 = 20² + 2a(50), so 0 = 400 + 100a, giving a = −4 m/s². The magnitude of the deceleration is 4 m/s².

questions.prompt: Why are small gaps left between the steel rails of a railway track?
options: To save steel and reduce cost
To allow the rails to expand when heated without buckling
To make the train run faster
questions.explanation: Steel expands when its temperature rises (thermal expansion). The gaps give the rails room to expand on hot days so they do not push against each other and buckle.

questions.prompt: Light from a flash of lightning is seen almost instantly, but the thunder is heard several seconds later. The best reason is that:
options: Light travels much faster than sound
Sound travels in a straight line but light does not
questions.explanation: Light travels at about 3 × 10⁸ m/s, far faster than sound at about 340 m/s. The sound therefore takes noticeably longer to reach you, causing the delay.

questions.prompt: A 6 Ω and a 6 Ω resistor are connected so that the supply voltage appears across each one separately and removing one does not switch off the other. How are they connected, and what is the voltage across each if the supply is 9 V?
questions.explanation: Components that each receive the full supply voltage and work independently are connected in parallel. So each 6 Ω resistor has the full 9 V across it.

questions.topic: Force and Newton's Laws of Motion
questions.prompt: A rocket pushes hot gas downward and the rocket moves upward. Which law explains this, and why does the rocket rise?
options: First Law; the rocket has inertia
Second Law; the gas has large mass
Third Law; the gas pushes back on the rocket with an equal and opposite force
Gravity; it pulls the rocket up
questions.explanation: By Newton's Third Law, the rocket pushes the gas down (action) and the gas pushes the rocket up with an equal and opposite force (reaction), driving the rocket upward.

questions.prompt: A straw in a glass of water looks bent at the water surface. This effect is caused by:
options: Reflection of light off the water
Refraction as light changes speed between water and air
Total absorption of light by water
The straw actually bending in water
questions.explanation: Light changes speed as it passes between water and air, so it bends (refracts) at the surface. This makes the straw appear bent even though it is straight.

questions.prompt: A student measures a fixed bar four times and gets 12.51 cm, 12.49 cm, 12.50 cm and 12.52 cm. The true length is 12.50 cm. These readings are best described as:
questions.explanation: The readings are very close to each other (precise) and their values cluster around the true value of 12.50 cm (accurate), so they are both accurate and precise.
